text:

title: YouTube: reach, virality and channel size
text:
Business context and hypotheses
Allocating editorial budgets and designing recommendation systems for video platforms require separating the inertia of a channel’s accumulated audience from content factors under the creator’s control. In the audited dataset of 12.00012.000 videos across 1515 editorial categories (viral_videos.csv), the binary virality indicator (viral = 1) is deterministically defined by the 8080th percentile (P80P_{80}) of view counts (views), with an exact boundary between 734.299734.299 and 734.379734.379 views (2.4002.400 viral videos and a base rate of 20,00%20,00\%).

Executive summary of the experiment

Structural dominance of the subscriber base (H1H_1 supported): The logarithmic subscriber count (ln⁡(1+subscriber_count)\ln(1 + \text{subscriber\_count})) has a correlation of r=0,8097r = 0,8097 (p<10−300p < 10^{-300}) with ln⁡(1+views)\ln(1 + \text{views}) and alone explains 65,56%65,56\% of total variance (R2=0,6556R^2 = 0,6556). In the pre-publication LightGBM model, channel size accounts for 93,59%93,59\% of total information gain in regression and 80,09%80,09\% in classification.
Simpson’s paradox in video duration (H2H_2 supported): The negative marginal correlation between duration_sec and ln⁡(1+views)\ln(1 + \text{views}) (r=−0,2015,p=3,97×10−110r = -0,2015, p = 3,97 \times 10^{-110}) arises from category confounding. Short-video categories (Music, with a median of 239s239\text{s} and 57,2%57,2\% virality; Comedy, with 297s297\text{s} and 35,2%35,2\%) contain channels 5x5\text{x} to 10x10\text{x} larger than long-video categories (Travel, Vlog). After normalizing by channel size (ln⁡(views/subscriber_count)\ln(\text{views}/\text{subscriber\_count})), the duration effect disappears (r=−0,0077,p=0,3966r = -0,0077, p = 0,3966).
Actionable creator factors in the simulation (H3H_3 supported): Including a human face in the thumbnail (thumbnail_face = 1) raises the virality rate from 18,15%18,15\% to 22,78%22,78\%, a relative increase of +25,52%+25,52\% (p=9,34×10−32p = 9,34 \times 10^{-32}), and increases the views-per-subscriber ratio by +24,39%+24,39\%. Indexing density through tags_count retains a positive correlation after adjustment for confounding (r=+0,0549,p=1,83×10−9r = +0,0549, p = 1,83 \times 10^{-9}).
Upload date and time neutrality (H4H_4 supported): Publication hour (upload_hour, Kruskal-Wallis p=0,6606p = 0,6606) and day of the week (upload_day, Kruskal-Wallis p=0,8717p = 0,8717) show no statistically significant effect on relative reach in this dataset.
Sufficiency of the pre-publication regime (H5H_5 supported): Adding six relative post-upload engagement rates (Regime B) changes the test PR-AUC by only +0,0051+0,0051 in LightGBM (0,7185→0,72370,7185 \to 0,7237) and leaves regression performance unchanged (RMSLE of 0,95840,9584 versus 0,95780,9578, p=0,8331p = 0,8331). The regularized linear model (LogisticRegression / Ridge) and dual convergence of the LGBMRegressor thresholded at quantile P80P_{80} achieve PR-AUC of 0,73830,7383 to 0,74090,7409 and ROC-AUC of 0,90720,9072 to 0,90940,9094 at upload time (cold start).



Central problem and audience skewness
Modeling digital attention metrics on their original scale produces unstable estimators. Raw view counts (views) range from 347347 to 158.516.795158.516.795, with a mean of 1.000.6421.000.642, median of 179.680179.680, positive skewness of +29,532+29,532 and excess kurtosis of 1.305,181.305,18. A single extreme observation in the right tail dominates ordinary squared loss.
Stabilization through the natural logarithmic transformation yreg=ln⁡(1+views)y_{\text{reg}} = \ln(1 + \text{views}) corrects this structural distortion. On the logarithmic scale, the distribution approaches a well-behaved Gaussian with a mean of 12,08912,089, standard deviation of 1,6361,636, skewness of +0,053+0,053 and excess kurtosis of +0,080+0,080. The subscriber base (subscriber_count) follows the same pattern: its skewness falls from +14,472+14,472 on the raw scale to +0,145+0,145 under ln⁡(1+subscriber_count)\ln(1 + \text{subscriber\_count}).


Falsifiable hypotheses (H1H_1 to H5H_5) and mathematical rationale for the metrics
The study follows five falsifiable hypotheses formulated before estimating the supervised models:

H1H_1 (Subscriber-base dominance): Logarithmic channel size alone accounts for more than 60%60\% of the variance of ln⁡(1+views)\ln(1 + \text{views}) and more than 75%75\% of information gain in tree-based models.
H2H_2 (Simpson’s paradox in duration): The apparent negative correlation between duration_sec and views (r<−0,18r < -0,18) results from confounding between editorial category and channel size, becoming negligible (|r|<0,02,p>0,05|r| < 0,02, p > 0,05) when evaluated against the multiplier ln⁡(views/subscriber_count)\ln(\text{views}/\text{subscriber\_count}).
H3H_3 (Creator packaging factors): thumbnail_face and tags_count retain a positive, statistically significant effect (p<0,001p < 0,001) after removing the effect of subscriber_count.
H4H_4 (Scheduling neutrality): upload_hour and upload_day have no significant effect (p>0,05p > 0,05) on view counts or the virality rate.
H5H_5 (Practical equivalence between cold start and relative post-upload signals): Adding relative engagement rates (likes/views, comments/views, shares/views) produces a marginal predictive gain below 0,0150,015 in PR-AUC and RMSLE compared with the model restricted to pre-upload metadata.

To respect the lognormal geometry of view counts and the minority prevalence of the positive class (20,0%20,0\%), the study uses two complementary metric families:

Continuous regression (y=ln⁡(1+views)y = \ln(1 + \text{views})): The primary metric is RMSLE (Root Mean Squared Logarithmic Error), accompanied by MAEln\text{MAE}_{\ln}, Rln⁡2R^2_{\ln} and MdAPE (Median Absolute Percentage Error on the original view-count scale). Because 𝔼[exp⁡(y)]≠exp⁡(𝔼[y])\mathbb{E}[\exp(y)] \neq \exp(\mathbb{E}[y]) under logarithmic residuals with finite variance, retransformation to count space applies the nonparametric smearing estimator from Duan, 1983:


V̂i=max⁡(0,ŝDuan⋅exp(ŷi)−1),where ŝDuan=1Ntr∑j=1Ntrexp⁡(yj−ŷj)\hat{V}_i = \max\left(0,\; \hat{s}_{\text{Duan}} \cdot \exp(\hat{y}_i) - 1\right), \quad \text{where } \hat{s}_{\text{Duan}} = \frac{1}{N_{\text{tr}}} \sum_{j=1}^{N_{\text{tr}}} \exp\left(y_j - \hat{y}_j\right)


Calibrated binary classification (ybin=𝕀[views≥734.379]y_{\text{bin}} = \mathbb{I}[\text{views} \ge 734.379]): The primary ranking metric is the area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC / Average Precision), whose random reference value equals the base rate π=0,2000\pi = 0,2000. The study also evaluates ROC-AUC, Brier Score (probability calibration) and F1@P80 (F1 evaluated at threshold τ80\tau_{80}, corresponding to the 8080th percentile of training-estimated probabilities and aligning the 20%20\% selection rate with the target’s structural definition).

Target and proxy leakage diagnostics (P80P_{80} and post-upload signals)
The statistical audit identified two information-leakage vectors that would invalidate a naive model using every column in the CSV file:

Deterministic target leakage (views ↔\leftrightarrow viral): The maximum view count among nonviral videos is 734.299734.299, while the minimum among viral videos is 734.379734.379. Because viral is an exact step function of views at quantile P80P_{80}, retaining views (or any monotonic transformation of views) in the classification predictor matrix XX produces artificial 100%100\% separation.
Proxy leakage in absolute engagement counts (likes, comments, shares): The dataset’s generation process simulated interactions by multiplying views by category-specific rates. Consequently, raw counts have logarithmic correlations of r=0,9736r = 0,9736 (likes), r=0,9601r = 0,9601 (comments) and r=0,9495r = 0,9495 (shares) with ln⁡(1+views)\ln(1 + \text{views}). Including raw engagement counts in XX gives the model a noisy copy of the response variable. In contrast, view-normalized rates (like_rate, comment_rate, share_rate) have virtually zero correlation with ln⁡(1+views)\ln(1 + \text{views}) (r∈[−0,0171;−0,0004]r \in [-0,0171;\, -0,0004]), separating qualitative engagement from the raw scale of reach.

Exploratory analysis and feature engineering
Following the principles of visual clarity and reduced cognitive load, the study’s five figures use aligned double panels (1x2, figsize=(12, 5.2), dpi=300, square box aspect ratio set_box_aspect(1)), connecting each business question to its statistical evidence.

Lognormal distributions and deterministic virality boundary (Figure 1)
Figure 1 documents the transition from the original long tail to logarithmic normality in Panel (a), and shows the coupling between channel size, view counts and the deterministic virality boundary (ln⁡(1+734.379)≈13,507\ln(1 + 734.379) \approx 13,507) in Panel (b).






Figure 1: Logarithmic stabilization (log1p) and deterministic virality boundary at quantile P80



Panel (b) supports Hypothesis H1H_1 within the simulation: the steep positive slope reflects the correlation of r=0,8097r = 0,8097 between ln⁡(1+subscriber_count)\ln(1 + \text{subscriber\_count}) and ln⁡(1+views)\ln(1 + \text{views}). Channels with more than 1 million1\text{ million} subscribers (ln⁡(1+subs)>13,8\ln(1 + \text{subs}) > 13,8) cross the horizontal line at 734.379734.379 views even when their videos perform below their own audience’s average in relative terms.


Decomposing Simpson’s paradox across categories and duration (Figure 2)
A superficial inspection would suggest that longer videos reduce reach (r=−0,2015,p=3,97×10−110r = -0,2015, p = 3,97 \times 10^{-110}). Figure 2 decomposes this phenomenon across the 1515 editorial categories.






Figure 2: Decomposition of Simpson’s paradox: category confounding versus duration neutrality



Panel (a) reveals the confounding structure: Music (57,2%57,2\% viral videos) and Comedy (35,2%35,2\%) have large median subscriber counts (2,06 million2,06\text{ million} and 850 thousand850\text{ thousand}) and short durations (239s239\text{s} and 297s297\text{s}). At the opposite end, Vlog, Food, DIY, Lifestyle and Travel have virality rates between 6,6%6,6\% and 9,4%9,4\% because their channels have median subscriber counts of 190 thousand190\text{ thousand} to 220 thousand220\text{ thousand}. When Panel (b) controls for the channel effect through standardized scores (Z-scores), the raw slope of r=−0,2015r = -0,2015 collapses to a horizontal line (r=−0,0077,p=0,3966r = -0,0077, p = 0,3966). In this simulated dataset, video duration neither reduces nor increases organic reach per subscriber.

Actionable creator factors and scheduling neutrality (Figure 3)
After adjusting for channel-size confounding, Figure 3 isolates the factors creators can control before publication.






Figure 3: Creator factors (thumbnail face and tags) versus upload-time neutrality in the simulation



Panel (a) supports Hypothesis H3H_3. Although channels using faces in thumbnails (thumbnail_face = 1, 40,0%40,0\% of the dataset) have the same median size as the others (≈381k\approx 381\text{k} subscribers), their virality rate rises from 18,15%18,15\% to 22,78%22,78\% (+25,52%+25,52\% relative; Welch’s tt test t=12,24,p=3,47×10−34t = 12,24, p = 3,47 \times 10^{-34}; Mann-Whitney p=9,34×10−32p = 9,34 \times 10^{-32}). The density distribution of tags_count also grows monotonically, raising the mean multiplier ln⁡(views/subs)\ln(\text{views}/\text{subs}) from −0,78-0,78 (0 to 5 tags) to −0,66-0,66 (21 to 30 tags; r=+0,0549,p=1,83×10−9r = +0,0549, p = 1,83 \times 10^{-9}).

The day of the week shows the same null pattern (Kruskal-Wallis H=2,47,p=0,8717H = 2,47, p = 0,8717).


Feature-regime specification (Regime A cold start versus Regime B relative signals)
To formally test Hypothesis H5H_5 without proxy leakage, the module src/youtube_viral/features.py builds two strictly separated feature matrices:

Regime A (Cold Start / Pre-publication, 18 features): Contains the 99 original features available before upload (category, subscriber_count, duration_sec, title_length, thumbnail_face, upload_hour, upload_day, tags_count, description_length) plus 99 deterministic domain transformations: log_subscriber_count (ln⁡(1+subs)\ln(1+\text{subs})), log_duration_sec (ln⁡(1+duration_sec)\ln(1+\text{duration\_sec})), tags_per_title_char, desc_to_title_ratio, cyclic hour encoding (hour_sin, hour_cos), the is_weekend indicator (Sat/Sun) and the has_tags and has_description flags.
Regime B (Relative Post-upload Early Signals, 24 features): Extends Regime A with 66 dimensionless engagement ratios: like_rate (likes/views\text{likes}/\text{views}), comment_rate (comments/views\text{comments}/\text{views}), share_rate (shares/views\text{shares}/\text{views}), engagement_rate_total ((likes+comments+shares)/views(\text{likes}+\text{comments}+\text{shares})/\text{views}), comments_per_like and shares_per_like. Contract DC-07 continues to block all raw counts.

title: YouTube: reach, virality and channel size
text:
Statistical modeling and machine learning

Stratified split protocol (80/20) and 5-fold cross-validation
The dataset of 12.00012.000 videos was deterministically partitioned (SEED = 42) into Training (Ntr=9.600N_{\text{tr}} = 9.600, 80%80\%) and Holdout test (Nte=2.400N_{\text{te}} = 2.400, 20%20\%) sets, using joint stratification by the composite key category + "_" + viral (3030 strata). The original report states that this design preserves the 20,00%20,00\% proportion of viral videos and the balance among the 1515 categories in both partitions, with internal cross-validation conducted over 55 stratified folds of the training set.


Three-part architecture: logarithmic regression, calibrated classification and confounding adjustment
The implementation in src/youtube_viral/modeling.py contains three complementary estimation tasks:

Task 1 (Logarithmic regression of ln⁡(1+views)\ln(1 + \text{views})): Compares a category-stratified baseline estimator (predicting the category’s historical mean of ln⁡(1+views)\ln(1 + \text{views}) within the training fold) against Ridge (α=1,0\alpha = 1,0 with StandardScaler and OneHotEncoder), RandomForestRegressor (300300 trees, max_depth=12) and LGBMRegressor (300300 trees, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8).
Task 2 (Calibrated binary classification and dual convergence at P80P_{80}): Compares the empirical category baseline against LogisticRegression (L2L_2, C=1,0C=1,0), RandomForestClassifier, LGBMClassifier and the hybrid estimator LightGBM_DualRegressor, which uses the LightGBM regressor’s continuous prediction ŷreg\hat{y}_{\text{reg}} to rank virality probability (through univariate logistic calibration) and applies the exact 8080th-percentile threshold (τ80\tau_{80}).
Task 3 (Confounding-adjusted organic-efficiency model): Trains a LGBMRegressor directly on the logarithmic multiplier M=ln⁡(views/subscriber_count)M = \ln(\text{views}/\text{subscriber\_count}), removing subscriber_count and log_subscriber_count from XX to isolate the contribution of content metadata.

text:
Executive recommendations and action plan
Within the educational simulation, the report translates the statistical evidence and audited models into the following decisions for content and recommendation-engineering teams. Applying them to a real platform would require validation with observational data and an appropriate evaluation design.

Tactical decision matrix for creators and platforms









Factor / system
Proposed action in the simulation
Quantified impact in the dataset




Thumbnail design (thumbnail_face)
Standardize expressive human faces in thumbnails across all editorial categories before upload.
Mean increase of −0,8280→−0,6097-0,8280 \to -0,6097 in ln⁡(views/subs)\ln(\text{views}/\text{subs}) (+24,4%+24,4\% in views per subscriber) and an increase of 18,15%→22,78%18,15\% \to 22,78\% in the probability of reaching the top 20%.


Semantic indexing (tags_count)
Fill in between 2020 and 3030 descriptive tags and maintain a balanced title-to-description ratio (tags_per_title_char).
Second-largest individual TreeSHAP contributor (|SHAP|=0,0321|\text{SHAP}| = 0,0321) to the organic-reach multiplier (r=+0,0549,p=1,83×10−9r = +0,0549, p = 1,83 \times 10^{-9}).


Duration (duration_sec) and scheduling (upload_hour/day)
Remove artificial duration cuts and publication-hour/day restrictions from the editorial calendar.
Duration has no detected effect on views per subscriber (r=−0,0077,p=0,3966r = -0,0077, p = 0,3966), and hours/days show a null effect (p>0,31p > 0,31) in the experiment.


Channel benchmarking (confounding adjustment)
Replace raw-view targets with the adjusted index M=ln⁡(views/subscriber_count)M = \ln(\text{views}/\text{subscriber\_count}), segmented by category.
Avoids penalizing niche categories (Vlog, Travel) or falsely rewarding giant channels in high-turnover categories (Music, Comedy) within the simulation.






Recommendation-system deployment scenario (cold start) and study limitations

Architecture proposed for the simulated scenario (Cold Start Scoring)

Inference at time zero (t = 0): Deploy the Ridge / LogisticRegression pair or LightGBM_DualRegressor, operating exclusively under Regime A (Cold Start) at video ingestion. Within this experiment, Regime A achieves PR-AUC = 0,7407 (LogisticRegression) and 0,7383 (LightGBM_DualRegressor), so waiting for post-upload engagement rates (Regime B, PR-AUC = 0,7409) offers little gain to justify the operational latency.
Decision rule calibrated at quantile P80P_{80}: Use the calibrated threshold τ80\tau_{80} (p≥0,4028p \ge 0,4028 for the logistic classifier or ŷreg≥13,2225\hat{y}_{\text{reg}} \ge 13,2225 for the dual regressor) instead of the naive 0,500,50 cutoff. In the experiment, this choice raises F1-Score from 0,63970,6397 to 0,67010,6701, with precision of 67,08%67,08\% and recall of 66,94%66,94\% in the promotional-prioritization queue.
Continuous contract guards (DC-01 to DC-07): Keep assert_no_leakage(X, regime="A") attached to the inference pipeline to prevent accidental introduction of raw interaction counts in future schema updates.

Methodological limitations and scope of generalization:

Synthetic, stationary dataset: The 12.00012.000 records come from a stationary parametric generator without external trend shocks, calendar seasonality or cross-video network effects. The report proposes evaluating view-growth velocity during the first two hours after upload (Δviews/Δt\Delta \text{views}/\Delta t) in real production data, monitored within strict time windows (Out-of-Time Validation); this experiment did not validate that additional signal.
Explanatory ceiling of tabular metadata without subscribers: As shown by the confounding-adjusted model in Task 3 (R² of 0,00460,0046 and RMSLE of 0,95000,9500 on ln⁡(views/subs)\ln(\text{views}/\text{subs})), superficial packaging metadata (thumbnail_face, tags_count, text lengths and category) capture statistically significant directional effects (p<10−30p < 10^{-30}) but leave much of the residual variance per subscriber unexplained. The report relates it to intrinsic audiovisual content quality and audience retention (watch time); because these variables are absent from this tabular schema, the experiment did not measure that explanation.

text:
NoteReport dated October 25, 2026, imported to the blog on November 5, 2026



This is a static import of the public report, without rerunning the analysis or performing new searches. Tables and figures preserve the published results. The narrative, captions and alternative text are translated; original figure labels remain in Portuguese, and numerical punctuation is preserved. The Quarto source and published HTML were archived separately, without verifying whether that HTML was generated from this exact source revision.
The project locates passages and reports their source file and line numbers so readers can check them. In the v2 test, positive queries are those with known references; BM25 found these references for more queries than the other methods. Negative queries ask for plausible details that do not appear in the inspected context. TF-IDF and BM25 returned passages for all of them.
The project demonstrates how to locate references when reading a collection and how a passage related to a topic can still fail to provide the requested detail. This workflow could help small teams that need to return to source documents when looking up information. The portfolio covers text preparation, method comparison and evaluation; the literature experiment does not measure performance on client documents.

From TXT files to verifiable references
The collection comes from the Sherlock Holmes Series dataset on Kaggle. The nine TXT files identify Arthur Conan Doyle and declare English in their headers. A list of identifiers calculated from the files, called hashes, makes it possible to check which files were used, as described in the provenance documentation.
Preparation reads the files as UTF-8, handles the BOM marker (which can appear at the beginning of a file) and line endings in memory, and preserves the originals. Editorial cuts remove credits, prefaces, tables of contents and footers identified during review. Each paragraph retains the work, file and source line range, including both endpoints. Line counting starts at 1 in the original TXT file. Internal editorial notes and some headings may remain because the project has no general routine for separating every story or chapter.

title: Sherlock Document Search: retrieval and its limits
section: Three methods over the same paragraphs
text:
Three methods over the same paragraphs
Each method can return up to five paragraphs, with their locations. Literal search looks for an exact sequence. TF-IDF turns terms into vectors and ranks paragraphs by cosine similarity, a measure of similarity between vectors. The implementation uses TfidfVectorizer(stop_words="english"), following the scikit-learn documentation. BM25 considers term frequency and paragraph length. The parameter k1=1,2 controls how much repeating a term increases its weight; b=0,75 controls length normalization. The Lucene documentation describes these parameters and the IDF formula used as a reference for the project’s own implementation.

title: Sherlock Document Search: retrieval and its limits
section: A test set separated before execution
text:
A test set separated before execution
During v2 development, 36 queries were assembled: 27 positive and nine negative. A different curator created the 24 final queries. Positive references come from different regions of the text, and a review checked for overlapping intents. The author approved both groups in the chat before freezing them. This record does not establish an individual human audit of each query.
The final evaluation uses 18 positive queries, divided equally among exact questions, paraphrases and context questions, plus six negative queries. A positive query has known references, although that list may be incomplete. A negative query asks for a plausible detail that does not appear in the inspected context. This review does not prove that the detail is absent from the entire collection.
The freeze at 14a0913 took place before the final run. Parameters, labels and editorial cuts were not changed afterward. The configuration decision records that a BM25 threshold of 32 was rejected during development: it eliminated all 12 known positive hits. In the final evaluation, BM25 only ranked the results, without an additional rule for declining to answer when evidence is insufficient.

The top-result diagnosis compares the passage’s topic with the requested attribute. Mentions of horses and a place do not provide ages; a delivery and an address do not indicate a price. Passages about a journey, South America, treasure or an attack may likewise fail to provide the fare, ship name, weight or caliber. These relationships help explain why the methods returned the passages even though they do not answer the questions.
A future version would need to treat ranking and the decision to decline an answer separately. It could test whether passages cover the requested attributes, whether there is a sufficient margin between candidates, or use an evaluator of question–passage pairs. Before tuning the methods, a new independent test would have to be reserved because the v2 sets have already been examined and published.

title: Fraudes bancárias: detecção, modalidades e perdas
text:
Resumo executivo
Este projeto estabelece um pipeline analítico ponta a ponta sobre 100.000 transações de cartão de crédito cobrindo o ano de 2026. Empregando uma arquitetura em três estágios (Hurdle Model), o sistema substitui abordagens tradicionais mono-estágio por um fluxo modular e auditável:

Detecção Binária (is_fraud): Priorização por PR-AUC com calibragem de limiar financeiro mínimo (C(t)=∑FN⋅Loss+$3,50⋅FPC(t) = \sum \text{FN} \cdot \text{Loss} + \$3,50 \cdot \text{FP}).
Tipificação de Fraude (fraud_type): Discriminação multiclasse entre 4 subtipos de ataque via Macro F1-Score.
Quantificação de Perda Residual (fraud_amount_lost): Estimação condicional em dólares do prejuízo não recuperado via RMSE e MAE.

section: Auditoria de Dados & Contratos (Data Understanding / Prepare)
text:
Auditoria de Dados & Contratos (Data Understanding / Prepare)
O relatório descreve os seguintes tratamentos para a base de 100.000 registros:

Preservação de Categoria Válida: O valor 'N/A' na coluna browser foi preservado para compras físicas presenciais (In-store) e caixas eletrônicos (ATM), totalizando 27.617 ocorrências legítimas e evitando imputações indevidas.
Ordenação Temporal Estável: Corrigiu-se a inversão pontual detectada em 28 de fevereiro de 2026, restabelecendo a sequência cronológica contínua.
Particionamento Out-of-Time Estrito: A divisão temporal garantiu isolamento completo de janelas futuras:
Treino: 01/01/2026 a 31/08/2026 (66.388 transações, 1.341 fraudes / 2,02%).
Validação: 01/09/2026 a 31/10/2026 (16.905 transações, 362 fraudes / 2,14%).
Teste Cego: 01/11/2026 a 31/12/2026 (16.707 transações, 352 fraudes / 2,11%).
Total Acumulado: 100.000 transações e 2.055 fraudes confirmadas (2,055% de prevalência).
Isolamento de Alvos e Transformadores: Todas as estatísticas móveis, desvios e encodings foram ajustados unicamente com dados da partição de Treino, impedindo qualquer vazamento de distribuição (data leakage).

text:
Análise Exploratória & Engenharia de Atributos (Data Prep & EDA / Process)
Para alimentar a modelagem preditiva, quatro famílias principais de atributos derivados foram desenvolvidas em src/features/pipeline.py:

Temporalidade Cíclica e Janela Crítica:

Decomposição periódica da hora em componentes ortogonais (sin⁡(2πh/24)\sin(2\pi h / 24) e cos⁡(2πh/24)\cos(2\pi h / 24)).
Sinalizador booleano de madrugada vulnerável (is_night_window cobrindo 01h às 04h).

Dinâmica Espacial e Salto Geográfico:

Estimativa da velocidade aparente de deslocamento entre a transação atual e a imediatamente anterior do mesmo cartão (Vaparente=distância/(Δt+0,1)V_{aparente} = \text{distância} / (\Delta t + 0,1) em km/h).

Desvio Comportamental de Consumo:

Razão do ticket sobre a média histórica de 30 dias (amount_vs_avg_ratio).
Escore padronizado de anomalia de gastos (Z=(amount−μ30d)/(σ30d+1)Z = (\text{amount} - \mu_{30d}) / (\sigma_{30d} + 1)).

Velocidade de Frequência e Alavancagem:

Indicador de disparada de compras em janela curta (transactions_last_1h >= 3).
Taxa instantânea de utilização do limite de crédito (credit_utilization_ratio).

title: Fraudes bancárias: detecção, modalidades e perdas
text:
Avaliação, Diagnóstico & Explicabilidade (Evaluation / Share)
Apresentamos a validação empírica detalhada respondendo às oito perguntas de negócio formuladas na Seção 1.

Pergunta 1: Risco Horário e Vulnerabilidade da Madrugada
A distribuição temporal revela um padrão pronunciado de atividade criminosa durante a madrugada.






Figura 1: Taxa de fraude horária e janela de alto risco na madrugada.



Enquanto o volume total de transações diminui consideravelmente entre 01h e 04h, a proporção de ataques atinge seu ápice em 8,5%, o que equivale a 4,15 vezes o baseline geral de 2,06% (Figura 1). O padrão observado neste conjunto não identifica seus mecanismos causais nem comprova comportamento de grupos criminosos.


Pergunta 2: Concentração Geográfica e Jurisdições Críticas
O país onde o terminal de captura está registrado atua como forte preditor de risco.






Figura 2: Taxa de incidência de fraude por país do lojista com baseline global.



Quatro jurisdições específicas (Rússia, Nigéria, Romênia e China) registram taxas médias de fraude de 11,1%, representando um multiplicador de 5,4x em relação aos países da União Europeia e América do Norte (Figura 2). Essas associações pertencem à base examinada; não justificam atribuir risco a pessoas ou países fora desse contexto.


Pergunta 3: Eficácia do Escudo EMV (Chip & PIN)
O estudo compara as taxas observadas em combinações de mecanismos de autenticação, sem identificar um efeito causal isolado do chip.






Figura 3: Comparativo de taxa de fraude por mecanismos de autenticação física e remota.



Transações presenciais que exigem conjuntamente a leitura do chip EMV e a digitação da senha numérica pessoal (PIN) apresentam taxa de fraude de apenas 0,78% (Figura 3). Por outro lado, transações digitais desprovidas de chip e senha exibem incidência de 3,46%, indicando uma associação entre o tipo de autenticação e a ocorrência de fraude nesta amostra.


Pergunta 4: Anomalias de Frequência e Ticket Médio
O comportamento recente da conta fornece sinais antecedentes decisivos.






Figura 4: Painel duplo mostrando o risco de fraude por volume transacional na última hora e razão em relação ao ticket médio.



O painel (a) de Figura 4 evidencia que clientes com três ou mais transações na mesma hora sofrem fraude em 5,6% das ocorrências (2,7x a média). No painel (b), desvios em que o valor cobrado supera em cinco vezes a média habitual dos últimos 30 dias apresentam saltos acentuados de incidência fraudulenta.


Pergunta 5: Curva Precision-Recall e Minimização de Custos
A calibração do threshold operacional sobre a base de validação out-of-time gerou as curvas características de desempenho financeiro.






Figura 5: Curva Precision-Recall (a) e curva de custo financeiro total em dólares (b).



O painel (a) de Figura 5 demonstra que o modelo sustenta precisão de 0,80 com recall próximo a 0,40, atingindo PR-AUC de 0,848. O painel (b) comprova que o ponto de mínimo custo financeiro ocorre em t*=0,170t^* = 0,170, bem abaixo do limiar simétrico de 0,50. Esse ponto de corte depende dos custos atribuídos aos erros no experimento, incluindo o custo de falsos alarmes ($3,50 por intervenção).


Pergunta 6: Explicabilidade Global via Valores SHAP
A auditoria regulatória e interna é suportada pela análise de atribuição aditiva de Shapley.






Figura 6: Ranking das 15 variáveis mais determinantes pelo ganho médio absoluto de SHAP.



Conforme ilustrado em Figura 6, os fatores que mais exercem pressão sobre o log-odds de fraude são:

amount_vs_avg_ratio: discrepância em relação ao consumo padrão.
transactions_last_1h: indicador de rajada transacional.
is_night_window: transações ocorridas entre 01h e 04h.
used_chip e used_pin: presença de autenticação forte como redutor de risco.
high_risk_country: registros provenientes de regiões de risco elevado.



Pergunta 7: Capacidade de Discriminação Multiclasse
A matriz de confusão do Estágio 2 avalia a separação entre as quatro formas de ataque detectadas.






Figura 7: Matriz de confusão normalizada por linha para o classificador multiclasse de tipos de fraude.



Como detalhado em Figura 7, modalidades como Card-Not-Present e Account-Takeover são identificadas com sensibilidade acima de 55%, ao passo que Synthetic-Identity apresenta maior sobreposição de padrões, justificando monitoramento especializado de abertura de cadastros.


Pergunta 8: Acurácia da Perda Monetária Prevista
O modelo do Estágio 3 estima o prejuízo remanescente caso a fraude não seja evitada a tempo.






Figura 8: Dispersão de perda real vs. prevista (a) e histograma de resíduos (b).



O painel (a) de Figura 8 exibe forte alinhamento com a reta diagonal de identidade (R2=0,929R^2 = 0,929), no conjunto de teste descrito pela fonte; isso não valida, por si só, o uso das estimativas para reservas de capital. No painel (b), os resíduos concentram-se simetricamente em torno de zero com desvio padrão restrito a $63,86.

section: Recomendações Executivas & Plano de Ação (Deployment / Act)
text:
Recomendações Executivas & Plano de Ação (Deployment / Act)
O relatório propõe os seguintes cenários operacionais. São recomendações do estudo para avaliação posterior; esta publicação não comprova sua eficácia em produção:

Gatilhos Automáticos de Autenticação Forte (Hard-Stop Noturno):

Transações que excedam 3x a média habitual de 30 dias executadas entre 01h e 04h devem ser imediatamente desafiadas por biometria facial ou token bancário antes da autorização.

Triagem Inteligente de Backoffice:

Casos com escore P(fraude)≥0,17P(\text{fraude}) \ge 0,17 e perda estimada superior a $250 devem ser alocados no topo da fila da equipe de análise de risco para contato preventivo com o portador em menos de 15 minutos.

Proteção Geográfica por Parâmetros de Risco:

Compras internacionais sem histórico prévio direcionadas a lojistas nos quatro países críticos devem acionar bloqueio preventivo temporário até confirmação expressa do cliente no aplicativo móvel.

Governança de Modelos e Monitoramento de Deriva (Drift):

Executar auditorias mensais de estabilidade populacional (Population Stability Index - PSI) sobre as variáveis de velocidade transacional e reavaliar trimestralmente o ponto de corte t*t^*.

text:
NotaImportação estática de 05/11/2026



Este estudo educacional usa dados sintéticos: os valores comerciais simulados não descrevem uma empresa real. O relatório original, datado de 16/10/2026, foi importado em 05/11/2026 com seus resultados estáticos, sem reexecutar análises. As afirmações de confirmação de hipóteses, causalidade e retorno financeiro pertencem ao relatório original e não foram reavaliadas nesta importação.
Este relatório consolida a investigação empírica sobre o ciclo de vida comercial e operacional do e-commerce entre 2021 e 2025. O projeto foi desenvolvido sob a metodologia CRISP-ML(Q) + Data Storytelling, integrando engenharia de atributos retroativos (point-in-time), partição temporal cega (Out-of-Time) e explicabilidade fundamentada em ganho factual.

title: E-commerce: vendas, clientes e risco operacional
text:
Contexto de Negócio e Hipóteses

Panorama Operacional: A Ilusão do Faturamento Bruto
Entre 01/01/2021 e 31/12/2025, o ecossistema de e-commerce transacionou $177.134.263,74 em faturamento líquido e $76.146.395,76 em lucro operacional. A operação mobilizou 138.116 pedidos distribuídos entre 24.911 clientes ativos, sustentando um ticket médio global (AOV) de $1.282,50.
À primeira vista, os indicadores agregados transmitem a imagem de uma operação consolidada. O volume transacional anual manteve-se estável, oscilando entre 27.554 e 27.768 pedidos por ano. A margem de contribuição média situou-se em 45,1%.
No entanto, a decomposição das transações revela três pontos cegos que limitam a rentabilidade sobre o capital investido:

Canibalização de Margem por Descontos Promocionais: Foram concedidos $32.819.346,82 em abatimentos no período. Políticas agressivas sem trava de segurança geraram vendas em que o custo do produto superou o faturamento, destruindo caixa diretamente.
Atrito Operacional em Cancelamentos e Devoluções: 17.860 pedidos não se converteram em receita efetiva (9.462 devoluções e 8.398 cancelamentos), atingindo 12,93% da base. Cada devolução acarreta frete reverso, recondicionamento e depreciação de inventário.
Miopia no Ciclo de Vida e Retorno de Aquisição: O investimento de marketing operou sem governança clara entre canais de alta retenção e fontes de tráfego de baixo valor agregado.

Hipóteses Centrais de Negócio
Para fundamentar o estudo, estruturamos cinco hipóteses empíricas:

H3H_3 (Risco Preventivo At-Purchase): É viável construir um modelo de classificação supervisionada que antecipe desfechos desfavoráveis (cancelamentos e devoluções) no momento da compra (At-Purchase), superando a taxa base de 12,93% sem utilizar variáveis de pós-venda.
H4H_4 (Concentração RFM): A base de clientes é altamente assimétrica, concentrando mais de 40% do faturamento no decil superior de compradores (Champions e Clientes Leais).

Auditoria de Dados e Contratos

Dicionário de Domínios e Consistência Contábil
A auditoria técnica examinou a base canônica ecommerce_sales_customer_analytics_150k.csv, composta por 138.116 linhas e 46 variáveis. O conjunto foi agrupado em cinco domínios funcionais:

Transacional & Temporal (4 variáveis): order_id (chave primária unívoca sem nulos), order_date (1.826 datas contínuas entre 2021-01-01 e 2025-12-31), order_time e order_status.
Cliente & Demografia (12 variáveis): customer_id (24.911 clientes únicos), dados demográficos (idade entre 18 e 74 anos, gênero), geografia (7 países, 5 regiões) e canal de venda.
Marketing & Campanhas (6 variáveis): Canal de origem (10 canais), campanhas, cupons promocionais e pontos de fidelidade.
Logística & Pós-Venda (9 variáveis): Métodos de pagamento, modalidade de envio, armazéns expedidores, tempos de entrega, status de devolução e avaliações.
Comercial & Precificação (15 variáveis): Quantidade, faturamento bruto, descontos, tributos, custos e margens.

A auditoria matemática comprovou duas identidades lineares que fecham no centavo:

net_sales=gross_sales−discount_amount+tax_amount+shipping_cost\text{net\_sales} = \text{gross\_sales} - \text{discount\_amount} + \text{tax\_amount} + \text{shipping\_cost}


profit=net_sales−shipping_cost−product_cost=(gross_sales−discount_amount+tax_amount)−product_cost\text{profit} = \text{net\_sales} - \text{shipping\_cost} - \text{product\_cost} = (\text{gross\_sales} - \text{discount\_amount} + \text{tax\_amount}) - \text{product\_cost}

Essa formulação revela uma particularidade do modelo de dados: a receita de frete é compensada pelo custo logístico, mas o valor de impostos (tax_amount) permanece na conta de lucro operacional da transação.

Anatomia do Vazamento de Dados (Data Leakage)
A investigação identificou frentes onde modelos ingênuos de machine learning aprenderiam atalhos triviais sem capacidade preditiva real em produção.
O infográfico abaixo (Figura 1) delimita a fronteira temporal estrita e o isolamento sistemático de variáveis adotado pelo pipeline para blindar o modelo contra vazamento de dados (Data Leakage):






Figura 1: Fronteira temporal estrita entre dados disponíveis no carrinho (At-Purchase) e variáveis descartadas de pós-venda (Data Leakage)




Vazamento de Alvo por Nulos Condicionais: As colunas delivery_days, estimated_delivery_days, customer_rating, review_sentiment e customer_review contêm 24.557 nulos. Esse volume corresponde à soma de pedidos cancelados (8.398), devolvidos (9.462) e pendentes (6.697). Um modelo que consumisse delivery_days aprenderia a regra espúria se delivery_days é nulo, o pedido não foi concluído.
Determinismo em Estados de Pagamento: 100% dos pedidos devolvidos possuem payment_status == 'Refunded' e 100% dos cancelados possuem payment_status == 'Failed'. Esses registros refletem o desfecho financeiro, inexistente no ato do checkout.
Vazamento Temporal Estático (Look-Ahead Leakage): O campo customer_lifetime_value foi computado considerando a receita total do cliente até o final de 2025. Se um pedido de 2021 usasse essa variável, estaria recebendo informações de transações futuras.
Artefato Sintético no Desconto: Transações canceladas e devolvidas apresentam desconto e pontos de fidelidade zerados no dataset original. Modelos expostos a essas colunas alcançam acurácia perfeita apenas decorando essa característica sintética.

Por esses motivos, o modelo preditivo foi blindado utilizando exclusivamente variáveis cadastrais, itens do carrinho e métricas retroativas calculadas ponto a ponto.

text:
Modelagem Estatística e Machine Learning

Formulação do Modelo Preventivo At-Purchase
Definimos a tarefa supervisionada como a identificação no ato da compra de pedidos com probabilidade de desfecho desfavorável:

y={1,se order_status∈{’Returned’,’Cancelled’}0,se order_status=’Completed’y = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{se } \text{order\_status} \in \{\text{'Returned'}, \text{'Cancelled'}\} \\ 0, & \text{se } \text{order\_status} = \text{'Completed'} \end{cases}

O problema caracteriza-se por um desbalanceamento moderado, com taxa positiva de 12,93% (17.860 pedidos desfavoráveis).
Para assegurar aplicação prática no checkout, a matriz de preditores utilizou estritamente:

Atributos Numéricos (9 variáveis): customer_age, quantity, gross_sales, tax_amount, shipping_cost, product_cost, orders_count_prior, spend_prior, days_since_last_order.
Atributos Categóricos (8 variáveis): gender, customer_segment, region, sales_channel, marketing_channel, payment_method, shipping_method, warehouse.



Protocolo de Validação Out-of-Time
A separação temporal estrita dividiu o histórico em:

Treino e Calibração (2021 a 2024): 110.518 pedidos (80,0%).
Teste Cego (2025): 27.598 pedidos (20,0%).

Comparamos dois estimadores:

Baseline Linear: Regressão Logística com pesos inversamente proporcionais às frequências das classes (class_weight='balanced') e regularização L2.
Modelo Baseado em Árvore: LightGBM Classifier com 100 estimadores, profundidade máxima 6, subsample = 0.8 e cálculo de importância por ganho real (importance_type='gain').

Recomendações Executivas e Plano de Ação

Simulador interativo de cenários what-if
Para explorar dinamicamente o impacto de descontos na margem de contribuição líquida, estimar o risco de devolução por prazo de frete e calcular o ponto de equilíbrio (break-even) da operação em tempo real, utilize a aplicação interativa:

Para execução local: uv run streamlit run app.py


Diretrizes estratégicas e simulação de retorno financeiro
Com base nos diagnósticos consolidados, propomos cinco intervenções prioritárias estruturadas por impacto financeiro e viabilidade operacional:

Governança de Pricing com Trava Rígida em 35% de Desconto:

Ação: Bloquear na plataforma de vendas cupons automáticos que concedam mais de 35% de desconto sobre o preço bruto. Descontos entre 35% e 50% passam a exigir aprovação da gerência comercial.
Impacto Financeiro: Recuperação de $201.225,34 em prejuízos acumulados nas 1.296 vendas deficitárias (economia média anual estimada em $40.245,00).

Realocação do Orçamento de Aquisição de Mídia:

Ação: Reduzir em 30% a alocação de verba em canais de menor retorno relativo (YouTube com LTV/CAC de 32,4x e TikTok com 33,7x). Redirecionar os recursos para iniciativas de SEO (Organic Search, com 50,5x) e busca direta (Google Ads, com 44,9x).
Impacto Financeiro: Ganho estimado de $180.000,00/ano em margem bruta adicional pelo aumento da proporção de clientes de alta recorrência.

Automação Preventiva de Risco no Checkout (Scoring com τ*=0,55\tau^* = 0,55):

Ação: Integrar o modelo LightGBM At-Purchase ao fluxo de checkout via microsserviço de inferência. Pedidos com probabilidade calculada superior a τ*=0,55\tau^* = 0,55 (limiar de custo mínimo) ativam dupla verificação de separação no centro de distribuição e checagem instantânea de endereço. Para categorias de vestuário e calçados, disparar prompt preventivo de confirmação de medidas.
Impacto Financeiro: Economia líquida de $92.495,00/ano na operação, reduzindo o custo de desfechos negativos de $161.910,00 para $69.415,00.

Saneamento Operacional de Armazém e Catálogo (Contenção de Devoluções):

Ação: Implementar leitura ótica bidimensional (bipagem 2D) obrigatória na expedição para neutralizar os 1.237 envios de produto errado (Wrong Product), atualizar o guia interativo de tamanhos (Size Issue) e auditar fornecedores de eletrônicos com taxas anômalas de avaria.
Impacto Financeiro: Redução de até 30% nas devoluções evitáveis, poupando $79.500,00/ano em fretes reversos e avarias físicas.

Régua de Reengajamento para a Coorte “At-Risk High-Value”:

Ação: Ativar campanhas personalizadas para os 8.670 clientes de alto valor histórico (gasto médio > $5.100) que não compram há mais de 400 dias.
Impacto Financeiro: Reativação de 4% dessa base (cerca de 347 clientes) representa um potencial de $445.000,00 em faturamento incremental.

section: 1. Ask Phase (Definição do Problema e Hipóteses)
text:
1. Ask Phase (Definição do Problema e Hipóteses)

1.1. Declaração da Tarefa de Negócio (Business Task)
A Cyclistic opera uma rede de 5.824 bicicletas distribuídas em 692 estações na cidade de Chicago. O modelo comercial oferece três modalidades de acesso: passes avulsos de corrida única (single-ride), passes diários (full-day) e assinaturas anuais. Clientes com passes avulsos ou diários são classificados como ciclistas casuais, enquanto contratantes do plano de 12 meses são membros anuais.
A diretoria financeira concluiu que os membros anuais geram significativamente maior margem operacional e estabilidade de fluxo de caixa do que ciclistas casuais. O objetivo deste estudo é:

Identificar com rigor estatístico como membros e casuais utilizam o serviço de forma divergente.
Determinar por que ciclistas casuais contratariam a assinatura anual.
Projetar recomendações de mídia digital e produto para converter ciclistas casuais em membros anuais.



1.2. Mapeamento de Stakeholders

Lily Moreno (Diretora de Marketing): Patrocinadora do projeto. Responsável pelas campanhas institucionais e canais digitais (e-mail, redes sociais e mídias de performance).
Equipe de Marketing Analytics: Analistas de dados responsáveis por coletar, transformar e modelar dados para respaldar decisões de investimento.
Comitê Executivo da Cyclistic: Colegiado responsável por aprovar o orçamento e as diretrizes operacionais do novo programa comercial.



1.3. Decomposição em Hipóteses Estatísticas Formais
Traduzimos as três perguntas centrais da diretoria em testes de hipóteses mensuráveis:

Pergunta 1 (Diferença de Comportamento):

H0H_0: As distribuições de duração e horários de deslocamento são idênticas entre membros anuais e ciclistas casuais.
H1H_1: Membros anuais apresentam tempos de viagem mais curtos com picos em horários comerciais, enquanto casuais exibem maior variância e concentração em fins de semana e tardes.

Pergunta 2 (Gatilhos de Adesão Anual):

H0H_0: O uso de ciclistas casuais é estritamente pontual e sem repetição semanal.
H1H_1: Existe um subgrupo relevante de ciclistas casuais com uso regular em dias úteis no trajeto casa-trabalho, para os quais o custo acumulado em passes avulsos supera a anuidade.

Pergunta 3 (Impacto da Mídia Digital):

H0H_0: Mensagens institucionais genéricas produzem a mesma taxa de resposta em qualquer horário ou estação.
H1H_1: Comunicações contextuais baseadas em geofencing e mensagens in-app disparadas após trajetos matinais recorrentes elevam a conversão.




1.4. Enquadramento Financeiro (Unit Economics)
Passes avulsos dependem de condições climáticas favoráveis. Chuvas e nevascas reduzem a receita transacional a quase zero no inverno de Chicago. A assinatura anual garante receita recorrente previsível, reduz o custo de aquisição por corrida e melhora a amortização dos custos fixos de manutenção da frota.

2. Prepare Phase (Origem, Governança ROCCC e Metadados)

2.1. Origem e Organização dos Dados
Os dados correspondem aos registros históricos de viagens do sistema Divvy de Chicago, operado pela Motivate International Inc. A base é organizada em 12 arquivos mensais em formato CSV, abrangendo variáveis temporais, espaciais, tipo de bicicleta e categoria do ciclista.


2.2. Avaliação de Confiabilidade pelo Framework ROCCC

Conforme

2.3. Licenciamento e Restrições de Privacidade (PII)
A licença proíbe expressamente a identificação de indivíduos. O conjunto de dados não armazena nomes, CPFs, números de cartão de crédito ou identificadores persistentes de usuários.

Implicação Metodológica: A unidade amostral é a viagem (ride_id), não o ciclista individual. Não é possível calcular diretamente a taxa de retenção por usuário sem identificador persistente. Para contornar essa restrição, analisamos padrões probabilísticos agregados de rotas recorrentes e janelas temporais de deslocamento.

section: 6. Act Phase (Recomendações Executivas, Teste A/B e Próximos Passos)
text:
6. Act Phase (Recomendações Executivas, Teste A/B e Próximos Passos)

6.1. Síntese Conclusiva
A análise comprova que a Cyclistic opera dois negócios paralelos na mesma malha:

Um serviço de mobilidade corporativa utilizado por membros anuais com alta previsibilidade e trajetos curtos em dias úteis.
Um serviço de lazer e turismo utilizado por ciclistas casuais com trajetos longos e concentração em fins de semana ensolarados.

A chave do crescimento financeiro não reside em tentar forçar o ciclista de lazer a pagar uma anuidade de inverno, mas em converter o segmento de Comutadores Ocultos (16.8% dos casuais) e criar produtos intermediários para o público recreativo.


6.2. As Três Recomendações Estratégicas

Recomendação 1: Campanha Digital Hiper-segmentada para o “Comutador Oculto”

Ação: Disparar notificações no aplicativo e e-mails automatizados exclusivamente para usuários que destravam bicicletas entre 7h-9h e 16h-18h em dias úteis.
Mecânica de Conversão: Exibir uma calculadora in-app: “Você realizou 4 viagens no horário comercial este mês. Com a assinatura anual, você teria economizado $18. Experimente o plano anual com crédito integral dos seus passes recentes.”
Incentivo: Reembolsar os passes avulsos adquiridos nos últimos 30 dias como desconto na anuidade.



Recomendação 2: Lançamento do Passe Sazonal de Primavera/Verão

Ação: O inverno de Chicago inibe a contratação de assinaturas de 12 meses para ciclistas de lazer. Criar um plano semestral (Maio a Outubro) voltado especificamente para a temporada de clima quente.
Objetivo: Capturar o excedente do público de lazer que rejeita o plano anual tradicional devido à ociosidade nos meses de frio rigoroso.



Recomendação 3: Ativação no Ponto de Uso em Estações Turísticas e Parques

Ação: Instalar totens com QR Codes e notificações por geofencing nas estações com maior volume de casuais (Streeter Dr & Grand Ave, Millennium Park e Theater on the Lake).
Mecânica: Oferecer upgrade com desconto imediatamente após o encerramento de corridas longas aos sábados e domingos.




6.3. Desenho Experimental do Teste A/B
Para validar a campanha do “Comutador Oculto” antes do lançamento nacional:

População do Teste: Ciclistas casuais que realizaram ≥3\ge 3 viagens em dias úteis nos horários de pico nos últimos 30 dias.
Divisão:

Grupo de Controle (50%): Recebe comunicação padrão de marketing sobre os benefícios institucionais da anuidade.
Grupo de Tratamento (50%): Recebe mensagem personalizada com calculadora de economia e crédito dos passes avulsos recentes aplicado à anuidade.

Métrica Primária: Taxa de conversão para assinatura anual em 30 dias.
Métrica Secundária: Taxa de renovação e churn após 6 meses.



6.4. Fontes Adicionais de Dados para Expansão Futura
Respondendo à questão final do roteiro da Google sobre dados complementares:

Dados Meteorológicos Horários da NOAA: Cruzar precipitação, sensação térmica e velocidade do vento por hora em Chicago para isolar a elasticidade-clima da demanda de cada grupo.
Integração com o Transporte Público de Chicago (CTA): Mapear a distância das estações da Cyclistic até as linhas de trem (‘L’) e ônibus, identificando rotas onde a bicicleta atua como complemento de primeira/última milha (first/last mile).

Pergunta e alcance
Como os registros de atividade, sono e frequência cardíaca variam nesta amostra de usuários Fitbit? O estudo usa esses dados como exercício exploratório no contexto de Bellabeat. Fitbit não é um produto Bellabeat, e o conjunto não identifica clientes dessa empresa.
A unidade de análise é o participante-dia. Uma mesma pessoa contribui com vários dias e pode aparecer em diferentes faixas de sono. As comparações descrevem os registros disponíveis; não identificam efeitos causais de sono, atividade ou intervenções comerciais.

title: Bellabeat: activity, sleep and fitness tracker usage
text:
Question and scope
How do activity, sleep and heart-rate records vary within this sample of Fitbit users? The study uses these data as an exploratory exercise in a Bellabeat business context. Fitbit is not a Bellabeat product, and the dataset does not identify that company’s customers.
The unit of analysis is the participant-day. One person contributes multiple days and may appear in different sleep categories. Comparisons describe available records; they do not identify causal effects of sleep, activity or commercial interventions.

text:
Corrected processing
The R script for this revision verifies the ZIP identity before reading the files and applies these rules:

Standardizes dates and verifies the participant-day key in each table.
Removes only exact duplicate sleep records. Distinct records sharing the same key fail validation rather than being discarded arbitrarily.
Aggregates heart-rate readings by participant-day and left-joins the tables to daily activity. The resulting table has 940 rows and 940 unique keys.
Converts minutes to hours, retaining total time in bed and creating a separate variable for time in bed minus time asleep.
Builds the long-form table directly, producing 3,760 rows without the previous many-to-many join.
Retains zeros and missing values. A zero is not assumed to prove actual inactivity, nor is missingness assumed to be random.

The previous version contained 943 rows; its long-form join implied 3,796 rows. The new summaries and figures use the corrected table rather than duplicated days.

title: Cyclistic Bike-Share: Usage Patterns and Rider Conversion
text:
Note



This is the October 13, 2026 version of the Bike Share project, incorporated into the blog on October 26, 2026. The complete report is translated below. Tables, charts and code were imported from the author’s rendered report, without rerunning the analysis or revalidating its statistical interpretations. This edition uses a different pipeline from the historical study; earlier versions remain available in the provenance section.

title: Cyclistic Bike-Share: Usage Patterns and Rider Conversion
text:
1. Ask Phase (Problem Definition and Hypotheses)

1.1. Business Task
Cyclistic operates a network of 5,824 bicycles distributed across 692 stations in Chicago. Its business model offers three access options: single-ride passes, full-day passes and annual subscriptions. Customers using single-ride or full-day passes are classified as casual riders, while those purchasing a 12-month plan are annual members.
The finance department concluded that annual members generate significantly higher operating margins and more stable cash flow than casual riders. This study aims to:

Identify, with statistical rigor, how members and casual riders use the service differently.
Determine why casual riders would purchase an annual subscription.
Develop digital media and product recommendations to convert casual riders into annual members.



1.2. Stakeholder Mapping

Lily Moreno (Marketing Director): Project sponsor, responsible for institutional campaigns and digital channels, including email, social media and performance marketing.
Marketing Analytics Team: Analysts responsible for collecting, transforming and modeling data to support investment decisions.
Cyclistic Executive Committee: The body responsible for approving the budget and operating guidelines of the new commercial program.



1.3. Formal Statistical Hypotheses
We translate management’s three central questions into measurable hypothesis tests:

Question 1 (Behavioral Differences):

H0H_0: Trip duration and departure-time distributions are identical for annual members and casual riders.
H1H_1: Annual members take shorter trips with peaks during business hours, while casual riders show greater variance and a concentration on weekends and afternoons.

Question 2 (Annual Subscription Triggers):

H0H_0: Casual riders use the service strictly on isolated occasions, with no weekly repetition.
H1H_1: A relevant subgroup of casual riders regularly travels on weekdays between home and work, and its accumulated single-ride pass costs exceed the annual subscription fee.

Question 3 (Digital Media Impact):

H0H_0: Generic institutional messages produce the same response rate regardless of time or season.
H1H_1: Contextual communications based on geofencing and in-app messages triggered after recurring morning trips increase conversion.




1.4. Unit Economics
Single-ride passes depend on favorable weather. Rain and snowstorms reduce transactional revenue to almost zero during Chicago’s winter. Annual subscriptions provide predictable recurring revenue, reduce acquisition cost per ride and improve the amortization of fixed fleet maintenance costs.

2. Prepare Phase (Sources, ROCCC Governance and Metadata)

2.1. Data Sources and Organization
The data consists of historical trips from Chicago’s Divvy system, operated by Motivate International Inc. The dataset is organized into 12 monthly CSV files covering temporal and spatial variables, bicycle type and rider category.


2.2. Reliability Assessment Using the ROCCC Framework

2.3. Licensing and Privacy Restrictions (PII)
The license expressly prohibits identifying individuals. The dataset does not store names, Brazilian taxpayer identification numbers (CPFs), credit card numbers or persistent user identifiers.

Methodological Implication: The observational unit is the trip (ride_id), rather than the individual rider. User retention cannot be calculated directly without a persistent identifier. To address this restriction, we analyze aggregate probabilistic patterns of recurring routes and travel time windows.

section: 6. Act Phase (Executive Recommendations, A/B Testing and Next Steps)
text:
6. Act Phase (Executive Recommendations, A/B Testing and Next Steps)

6.1. Conclusions
The analysis demonstrates that Cyclistic operates two parallel businesses on the same network:

A business mobility service used by annual members with high predictability and short weekday trips.
A leisure and tourism service used by casual riders, with longer trips concentrated on sunny weekends.

The key to financial growth is to convert Hidden Commuters (16.8% of casual trips) and create intermediate products for recreational riders, rather than trying to persuade leisure riders to pay for an annual winter subscription.


6.2. Three Strategic Recommendations

Recommendation 1: Highly Targeted Digital Campaign for the “Hidden Commuter”

Action: Send in-app notifications and automated emails exclusively to users who unlock bicycles between 7–9 a.m. and 4–6 p.m. on weekdays.
Conversion Mechanism: Display an in-app calculator: “You took 4 trips during business hours this month. With an annual subscription, you would have saved $18. Try the annual plan with full credit for your recent passes.”
Incentive: Refund single-ride passes purchased in the past 30 days as a discount on the annual subscription.



Recommendation 2: Launch a Spring/Summer Seasonal Pass

Action: Chicago’s winter discourages 12-month subscriptions among leisure riders. Create a six-month plan (May through October) specifically for the warm-weather season.
Objective: Capture additional demand from leisure riders who reject the traditional annual plan because of inactivity during the harsh winter months.



Recommendation 3: Point-of-Use Activation at Tourist Stations and Parks

Action: Install QR-code displays and geofencing notifications at stations with the highest casual trip volumes (Streeter Dr & Grand Ave, Millennium Park and Theater on the Lake).
Mechanism: Offer a discounted upgrade immediately after long rides end on Saturdays and Sundays.




6.3. A/B Test Design
To validate the “Hidden Commuter” campaign before a nationwide launch:

Test Population: Casual riders who made ≥3\ge 3 weekday trips during commuting hours in the past 30 days.
Assignment:

Control Group (50%): Receives standard marketing communications about the annual subscription’s institutional benefits.
Treatment Group (50%): Receives a personalized message with a savings calculator and credit for recent single-ride passes applied to the annual subscription.

Primary Metric: Conversion to an annual subscription within 30 days.
Secondary Metric: Renewal and churn after 6 months.



6.4. Additional Data Sources for Future Expansion
To address the final question in Google’s case study regarding complementary data:

NOAA Hourly Weather Data: Combine hourly precipitation, apparent temperature and wind speed in Chicago to isolate each group’s demand elasticity with respect to weather.
Integration with Chicago Public Transit (CTA): Map the distance between Cyclistic stations and train (‘L’) and bus lines to identify routes where bicycles provide first/last-mile transport.

title: E-commerce: sales, customers and operational risk
text:
Business context and hypotheses

Operational overview: the illusion of gross revenue
Between 01/01/2021 and 31/12/2025, the e-commerce operation generated $177.134.263,74 in net sales and $76.146.395,76 in operating profit. It handled 138.116 orders from 24.911 active customers, with an overall average order value (AOV) of $1.282,50.
At first glance, the aggregate indicators suggest an established operation. Annual transaction volume remained stable, ranging from 27.554 to 27.768 orders per year. The average contribution margin was 45,1%.
However, breaking down the transactions reveals three blind spots that limit the return on invested capital:

Margin erosion from promotional discounts: Discounts totaled $32.819.346,82 over the period. Aggressive policies without safeguards produced sales in which product costs exceeded revenue, directly consuming cash.
Operational friction from cancellations and returns: 17.860 orders failed to generate realized revenue (9.462 returns and 8.398 cancellations), representing 12,93% of the dataset. Each return entails reverse shipping, refurbishment and inventory depreciation.
Limited visibility into the customer lifecycle and acquisition returns: Marketing spending lacked clear governance to distinguish high-retention channels from lower-value traffic sources.

Main business hypotheses
The study was organized around five empirical hypotheses:

H1H_1 (Discount-related margin inflection): The relationship between discount percentage and profit margin has an inflection point at D*∈[35%,40%]D^* \in [35\%, 40\%]. Above this threshold, discounts exceed the catalog’s commercial margin, producing loss-making sales with negative margins.
H2H_2 (LTV / CAC acquisition efficiency): Organic and direct channels (Organic Search, Direct) offer an LTV/CAC ratio at least 25% higher than paid media (Google Ads, Facebook Ads) and social networks (TikTok, YouTube).
H3H_3 (Preventive at-purchase risk): A supervised classifier can anticipate unfavorable outcomes (cancellations and returns) at the time of purchase (At-Purchase), outperforming the 12,93% base rate without using post-sale variables.
H4H_4 (RFM concentration): The customer base is highly uneven, with more than 40% of revenue concentrated in the top decile of buyers (Champions and Loyal Customers).
H5H_5 (Delivery-delay penalty): Completed orders delivered later than the estimate communicated to the buyer receive a statistically significant penalty (≥0,5\ge 0,5 stars) in their post-sale rating (customer_rating).

title: E-commerce: sales, customers and operational risk
text:
Data audit and contracts

Domain dictionary and accounting consistency
The technical audit examined the canonical dataset ecommerce_sales_customer_analytics_150k.csv, containing 138.116 rows and 46 variables. These were organized into five functional domains:

Transactions and time (4 variables): order_id (a unique primary key with no missing values), order_date (1.826 consecutive dates between 2021-01-01 and 2025-12-31), order_time and order_status.
Customers and demographics (12 variables): customer_id (24.911 unique customers), demographics (age between 18 and 74, gender), geography (7 countries, 5 regions) and sales channel.
Marketing and campaigns (6 variables): Acquisition channel (10 channels), campaigns, promotional coupons and loyalty points.
Logistics and post-sale service (9 variables): Payment methods, shipping methods, dispatch warehouses, delivery times, return status and ratings.
Sales and pricing (15 variables): Quantity, gross sales, discounts, taxes, costs and margins.

The mathematical audit reported two linear identities that reconcile to the cent:

net_sales=gross_sales−discount_amount+tax_amount+shipping_cost\text{net\_sales} = \text{gross\_sales} - \text{discount\_amount} + \text{tax\_amount} + \text{shipping\_cost}


profit=net_sales−shipping_cost−product_cost=(gross_sales−discount_amount+tax_amount)−product_cost\text{profit} = \text{net\_sales} - \text{shipping\_cost} - \text{product\_cost} = (\text{gross\_sales} - \text{discount\_amount} + \text{tax\_amount}) - \text{product\_cost}

This formulation reveals a particular feature of the data model: shipping revenue is offset by logistics costs, while tax amounts (tax_amount) remain included in the transaction’s operating profit.


Methodological stages and adopted gates
The project followed the Archetype A (Data Science, Analytics & Machine Learning) development workflow, organized into two sequential phases: planning before coding through five governance gates, followed by modular technical implementation guided by unit tests (TDD).

Anatomy of data leakage
The investigation identified several ways in which naive machine learning models could learn trivial shortcuts without useful predictive ability in production.
The infographic below (Figure 1) sets out the strict temporal boundary and variable isolation used by the pipeline to protect the model against data leakage:






Figure 1: Strict temporal boundary between information available in the cart (At-Purchase) and excluded post-sale variables (Data Leakage)




Target leakage through conditional missing values: The columns delivery_days, estimated_delivery_days, customer_rating, review_sentiment and customer_review contain 24.557 missing values. This matches the sum of cancelled (8.398), returned (9.462) and pending (6.697) orders. A model using delivery_days would learn the spurious rule se delivery_days é nulo, o pedido não foi concluído.
Deterministic payment states: 100% of returned orders have payment_status == 'Refunded' and 100% of cancelled orders have payment_status == 'Failed'. These records reflect the financial outcome, which is unavailable at checkout.
Static temporal leakage (look-ahead leakage): customer_lifetime_value was calculated from each customer’s total revenue through the end of 2025. Using this variable for a 2021 order would expose the model to future transactions.
Synthetic discount artifact: Cancelled and returned transactions have zero discounts and loyalty points in the original dataset. Models exposed to these columns achieve perfect accuracy simply by memorizing this synthetic pattern.

For these reasons, the predictive model used only customer attributes, cart contents and historical metrics calculated at each point in time.

Statistical modeling and machine learning

Formulating the preventive at-purchase model
The supervised task was defined as identifying, at purchase, orders likely to have an unfavorable outcome:

y={1,if order_status∈{’Returned’,’Cancelled’}0,if order_status=’Completed’y = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if } \text{order\_status} \in \{\text{'Returned'}, \text{'Cancelled'}\} \\ 0, & \text{if } \text{order\_status} = \text{'Completed'} \end{cases}

The problem has moderate class imbalance, with a positive rate of 12,93% (17.860 unfavorable orders).
To support use at checkout, the predictor matrix was restricted to:

Numerical features (9 variables): customer_age, quantity, gross_sales, tax_amount, shipping_cost, product_cost, orders_count_prior, spend_prior, days_since_last_order.
Categorical features (8 variables): gender, customer_segment, region, sales_channel, marketing_channel, payment_method, shipping_method, warehouse.



Out-of-time validation protocol
The strict temporal split divided the historical data into:

Training and calibration (2021 to 2024): 110.518 orders (80,0%).
Blind test (2025): 27.598 orders (20,0%).

Two estimators were compared:

Linear baseline: Logistic regression with weights inversely proportional to class frequencies (class_weight='balanced') and L2 regularization.
Tree-based model: A LightGBM classifier with 100 estimators, a maximum depth of 6, subsample = 0.8 and gain-based feature importance (importance_type='gain').

Probabilistic reliability was assessed using the Brier Score and the reliability curve. LightGBM achieved a Brier Score of 0,0893, outperforming logistic regression (0,2291) and the historical marginal probability (0,1125).

Executive recommendations and action plan

Interactive what-if scenario simulator
To explore the effect of discounts on net contribution margin, estimate return risk by shipping time and calculate the operation’s break-even point dynamically, use the interactive application:
Open the what-if simulator (Streamlit Cloud)
To run locally: uv run streamlit run app.py


Strategic guidelines and simulated financial returns
Based on the combined diagnostics, the report proposes five priority interventions organized by financial impact and operational feasibility:

Pricing governance with a strict 35% discount safeguard:

Action: Block automatic coupons granting more than 35% off the gross price on the sales platform. Discounts between 35% and 50% would require commercial management approval.
Financial impact: Recover $201.225,34 in cumulative losses from the 1.296 loss-making sales (estimated average annual savings of $40.245,00).

Reallocate the paid-acquisition budget:

Action: Reduce spending on lower-return channels by 30% (YouTube with LTV/CAC of 32,4x and TikTok with 33,7x). Redirect resources to SEO initiatives (Organic Search, at 50,5x) and direct search (Google Ads, at 44,9x).
Financial impact: An estimated $180.000,00/year in additional gross margin from increasing the share of frequently returning customers.

Preventive checkout risk automation (scoring at τ*=0,55\tau^* = 0,55):

Action: Integrate the LightGBM At-Purchase model into checkout through an inference microservice. Orders with predicted probabilities above τ*=0,55\tau^* = 0,55 (the minimum-cost threshold) would trigger a second picking check at the distribution center and an immediate address check. For clothing and footwear, trigger a preventive prompt to confirm measurements.
Financial impact: Net savings of $92.495,00/year, reducing the cost of unfavorable outcomes from $161.910,00 to $69.415,00.

Warehouse and catalog improvements to contain returns:

Action: Require two-dimensional barcode scanning (2D scanning) at dispatch to prevent the 1.237 wrong-product shipments (Wrong Product), update the interactive size guide (Size Issue) and audit electronics suppliers with anomalous damage rates.
Financial impact: Reduce avoidable returns by up to 30%, saving $79.500,00/year in reverse shipping and physical damage.

A re-engagement sequence for the “At-Risk High-Value” cohort:

Action: Launch personalized campaigns for the 8.670 historically high-value customers (average spending > $5.100) who have not purchased for more than 400 days.
Financial impact: Reactivating 4% of this group (approximately 347 customers) represents potential incremental revenue of $445.000,00.

title: Banking fraud: detection, fraud types and losses
text:
Executive summary
This project establishes an end-to-end analytical pipeline over 100.000 credit card transactions covering 2026. Using a three-stage architecture (Hurdle Model), the system replaces traditional single-stage approaches with a modular, auditable workflow:

Binary detection (is_fraud): Prioritization by PR-AUC, with threshold calibration to minimize financial cost (C(t)=∑FN⋅Loss+$3,50⋅FPC(t) = \sum \text{FN} \cdot \text{Loss} + \$3,50 \cdot \text{FP}).
Fraud classification (fraud_type): Multiclass discrimination among 4 attack subtypes using Macro F1-Score.
Residual loss estimation (fraud_amount_lost): Conditional estimation in dollars of unrecovered losses, evaluated with RMSE and MAE.

text:
Data audit and contracts (Data Understanding / Prepare)
The report describes the following treatments for the dataset of 100.000 records:

Preserving a valid category: The value 'N/A' in the browser column was retained for physical purchases (In-store) and cash machines (ATM), totaling 27.617 legitimate occurrences and avoiding inappropriate imputation.
Stable chronological ordering: A local ordering reversal detected on February 28, 2026 was corrected, restoring a continuous chronological sequence.
Strict out-of-time splits: The temporal split fully isolated future windows:
Training: 01/01/2026 to 31/08/2026 (66.388 transactions, 1.341 fraud cases / 2,02%).
Validation: 01/09/2026 to 31/10/2026 (16.905 transactions, 362 fraud cases / 2,14%).
Blind test: 01/11/2026 to 31/12/2026 (16.707 transactions, 352 fraud cases / 2,11%).
Overall total: 100.000 transactions and 2.055 confirmed fraud cases (2,055% prevalence).
Isolation of targets and transformers: All rolling statistics, deviations and encodings were fitted using only training-partition data, preventing distribution leakage (data leakage).

Exploratory analysis and feature engineering (Data Prep & EDA / Process)
Four main families of derived features were developed in src/features/pipeline.py to support predictive modeling:

Cyclical time and the critical window:

Periodic decomposition of the hour into orthogonal components (sin⁡(2πh/24)\sin(2\pi h / 24) and cos⁡(2πh/24)\cos(2\pi h / 24)).
Boolean indicator for the vulnerable overnight window (is_night_window, covering 01h to 04h).

Spatial dynamics and geographic jumps:

Estimated apparent travel speed between the current transaction and the immediately preceding transaction on the same card (Vaparente=distância/(Δt+0,1)V_{aparente} = \text{distância} / (\Delta t + 0,1) in km/h).

Behavioral spending deviations:

Ratio of the purchase amount to the historical 30-day mean (amount_vs_avg_ratio).
Standardized spending-anomaly score (Z=(amount−μ30d)/(σ30d+1)Z = (\text{amount} - \mu_{30d}) / (\sigma_{30d} + 1)).

Transaction frequency and credit usage:

Indicator of a purchase burst within a short window (transactions_last_1h >= 3).
Instantaneous credit-limit utilization ratio (credit_utilization_ratio).
